identity.title: Spatially Resolved <SUP>12</SUP>CO(2-1)/<SUP>12</SUP>CO(1-0) in the Starburst Galaxy NGC 253: Assessing Optical Depth to Constrain the Molecular Mass Outflow Rate

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of $^{12}$CO(1–0) and $^{12}$CO(2–1) in the central 40$''$ (680 pc) of the nuclear starburst galaxy NGC 253

evidence.quote: At a distance of 3.5 Mpc (cite: 2005MNRAS.361..330R), with a systemic velocity of 243 km s$^{-1}$, NGC 253 is the nearest nuclear starburst galaxy in the Southern sky

evidence.quote: to determine whether or not the CO emission observed in the outflow of NGC 253 is optically-thick

findings_qualitative.value: r21 under unity throughout, attributed to temperature gradients in optically thick gas

evidence.quote: We attribute this to temperature gradients in the optically thick emitting gas.

claims.hypothesis: CO in the NGC 253 outflow is optically thick
claims.experiment: Measured r21 in disk, SW streamer and outflow features
claims.result: r21 between 0.5 and 1.0, no optically thin values
claims.finding: CO emission is mostly optically thick in the outflow as in the starburst

evidence.quote: The most natural conclusion is that the majority of the molecular gas has conditions such that the CO emission is also optically thick

claims.hypothesis: Optically thin assumption underestimates outflow mass
claims.experiment: Rescaled Bolatto 2013 estimates with starburst alpha_CO
claims.finding: Outflow rate 3-6 times the lower limit

evidence.quote: The implied molecular mass outflow rate is $25-50$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$, assuming that conversion factor for the outflowing gas is similar

claims.hypothesis: The extended CO(2-1) component is real
claims.experiment: TP flagging, baseline fitting, and comparison
claims.finding: Tentatively real, biconical like ionized wind

evidence.quote: Ultimately, we are unable to demonstrate that the extended emission is an artifact.

why_this_method.value: 13CO too faint in outflow, so use r21 for optical depth

evidence.quote: However, $^{13}$CO is difficult to detect in relatively faint outflow features.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Subthermal excitation or cold gas rejected as cause of low r21

evidence.quote: This departure is not due to subthermal excitation, or exceedingly cold gas temperatures.

limitations_admitted.value: Regions near the map edge may have artificially low r21 from poor flux recovery

evidence.quote: In these cases $r_{21}$ could be artificially low.

limitations_admitted.value: Large uncertainties in alpha_CO, geometry and apportioning of CO to outflow

evidence.quote: there are considerable uncertainties associated with these values beyond the adoption of a conversion factor

referee_caveats_inferred: Mass rate relies on applying central-starburst alpha_CO to the outflow without independent check
Thresholds (70% mask, 30 km/s windows) are arbitrary and no uncertainty propagation on r21 beyond 2 sigma
Extended component may be a TP combination artifact
